findings.title: AC-24 and AC-9 put T-30 in the changed list, but CT-6 and TC-20 keep the changed IDs empty
quotes: T-30 is in the changed list; the lenses-to-re-run list is empty.
the judged changed IDs are `[]` and the lenses to re-run `[]`
T-30 is among the changed IDs it reports.
the `changed:` line keeps only judged IDs
findings.fix: state in AC-9 and AC-24 that added fix tasks are listed on the `added under Fixes:` line and are not in `changed:`, and make TC-9 and TC-20 match that wording.

sources.situation: T-9 implements CT-6 and prints `changed: T-4` with `added under Fixes: T-30` on its own line. That passes TC-9. A reader of AC-24 expects T-30 inside the changed list, and TC-20 asserts the judged changed IDs are `[]`. If the worker puts T-30 into `changed:`, TC-20 fails. If it doesn't, AC-24's observable is unmet unless the separate line counts as the list. Two outcomes from the same fixture are possible, and the spec picks neither.

findings.reason: CT-6 (contracts.md:53) says the `added under Fixes:` line is the list FR-7 asks for and that `changed:` keeps only judged IDs. TC-9 (tests.md:70) and TC-20 (tests.md:147) both assert exactly that, so a worker has one outcome. AC-9 and AC-24 still say "changed IDs/list" loosely, but the plan gate already judged and fixed this point (plan ledger J-2, fixed).

findings.title: T-3 names no test file and has no owner for its check, and its Tier cites an example that is not in tasks.md
quotes: - Test: a direct unit check calling `own`; TC-19 proved later by T-4
- Mode: single: tiny function, one worker writes check and code
`tasks.own("TC-38, plus a direct check; TC-38 proved later by T-11") == ["TC-38"]`
findings.fix: add the file that holds the direct check to T-3's Files and give the example input and expected list in T-3's Test line. Say that the TC-19 assertion on `own` belongs to T-4.

sources.situation: the worker writes `own` and its direct check. Files lists only src/nio/tasks.py, so the check either lands in an unlisted tests/test_tasks.py, which breaks "names every file it changes", or in tests/test_implement.py beside TC-19's own assertion, which belongs to T-4's Files. The Tier claims "a stated example", but tasks.md states none. The only example is in tests.md TC-19. Two workers could each think the other writes it, or neither does.

findings.reason: T-3 lists only `src/nio/tasks.py` in Files, yet its Test line asks for "a direct unit check calling `own`". That check needs a test file, which is neither listed in T-3 nor assigned to T-4 (T-4's `tests/test_implement.py` assertion is TC-19). tasks.md also states no example for the "stated example" in the Tier. The only `own` example is in tests.md TC-19 (line 140).
findings.note: T-3 Files adds tests/test_tasks.py; its Test line names test_own and the three example lines from TC-4, TC-6 and TC-19; T-4 owns TC-19's red assertion.

findings.title: T-4 says TC-27 fails today, but its assertion looks like it passes on today's code
quotes: TC-5, TC-6, TC-7, TC-19, TC-27 fail today, so red can be proved
findings.fix: remove TC-27 from the "fail today" list and mark it as a guard, as TC-14 is in T-5.

sources.situation: TC-27 runs red with tests/test_z.py, which names no TC file. Today's refusal names the files of the task's TC IDs, which include tests/test_a.py, so exit 1 naming tests/test_a.py already holds today. The worker sees TC-27 pass before any change, and the Mode claim looks wrong. I could not confirm today's refusal wording from the artefacts, so this is inferred. The split still holds through TC-5, TC-6, TC-7 and TC-19.

findings.note: T-4's Mode reason now lists TC-27 with TC-4 and TC-18 as regression guards.

findings.title: T-5 is rated Effort low, but its own Tier note says the tests need an elaborate fixture
quotes: - Tier: strong: small env change, tests need an elaborate fixture
findings.fix: rate T-5 Effort med, or cut the fixture note from the Tier line.

sources.situation: TC-13 needs a claimed T-1, a baseline run with NIO_PERF unset, then NIO_PERF set mid-test before green. TC-30 needs the same fixture. A worker rating the fixture as low effort may skip the mid-test env switch and so write a test that passes for the wrong reason. The rating doesn't match the work it describes.

findings.title: T-13 drops the failure path the contract gives the skill, so a failed --rated-from has no instruction
quotes: ### T-13 Make the tasks skill copy `tasks.md` before the evaluator and run `--rated-from` after
sending a failure back to the evaluator once
findings.fix: copy the CT-11 failure step into T-13 (the copy path under .nio/runs/<run>/ and one return to the evaluator) and extend TC-24 to assert the retry line.

sources.situation: the evaluator edits tasks.md and the check then fails on a non-rating line. T-13's text has no step for that, and TC-24 checks only the order of copy and run. Whether the skill sends the failure back once or accepts the file depends on the worker reading CT-11. A worker that reads only T-13 might let the file pass or edit it by hand, which is the outcome US-4 forbids.

findings.note: T-13's Test line now carries CT-11's run, copy path and one return to the evaluator.
